readability.reads_as: a small dip with the strip rolling ~60 deg each way: more a head tilt than a nod
readability.note: The TCP dips 0.13 m (0.59 -> 0.46 m at 1.5-2.2 s, back by 3.0 s): a nod is meant small. But on each dip the strip windmills (J6 range 63 deg, joint share J6 0.54; strip tip 1.25 m/s vs TCP 0.30; AUDIENCE SIDE ghosts 4-7 go from upright to near level). The strip's lower end stays 0.12-0.18 m over the floor through the dip while the TCP drops 0.13 m: the roll is the strip being turned off the floor (strip_safe), not the gaze. The only clearly 'nod' cue is the TCP dip; the second, smaller nod (3.4-3.6 s) is a 0.13 m/s blip.

awkward.evidence: J6 range 63 deg, strip tip 1.25 m/s vs TCP 0.30 m/s; strip lower end held at 0.12-0.18 m (show.strip_ends) during the dip
isolated J5 accel spike 62 % (J4 ~50 %) against ~10 % speed, on a 0.13 m/s blip

audience.note: Seen from AUDIENCE SIDE, but the dominant image is the strip rolling in the frontal plane, the same image as low_04_tilt.
